page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high-clock-speed hfc5 family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The underlying x86_64 microarchitecture incorporates support for AVX-512F vector extensions, FMA, and AES hardware encryption, alongside 22 MB of shared L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core.

System memory consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks for persistent filesystem volumes. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Hardware acceleration is absent, with a zero GPU profile.

Benchmark assessments show solid mid-tier performance across parallel processing workloads, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 6654.0 and a PassMark CPU aggregate of 15463.52. Memory operations remain stable, yielding a cached small-block read bandwidth of 804.1 GB/sec and uncached large-block read transfers of 73.32 GB/sec. However, single-core execution reflects older microarchitecture limitations, resulting in lower relative single-thread metrics such as a 1095.0 Geekbench single-core score and modest single-threaded compression throughput.

Due to its balanced compute-to-RAM density and predictable dedicated CPU assignment, the ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is best suited for concurrent multi-threaded workloads. Practical applications include software compilation, web serving clusters, intermediate batch data processing, distributed caching services like Redis, and continuous integration runners.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.4xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 32.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and 22 MB of L3 cache, with AVX-512F instruction support. The instance operates without bundled local disks, relying on external network storage, and provides a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth with no hardware GPU acceleration. Performance testing shows average multi-core processing throughput, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 15463.52 and steady memory transfer rates, though single-core execution metrics lag behind modern standards. The instance offers a practical hardware profile for multi-threaded batch jobs, CI/CD pipelines, web serving tiers, and in-memory caching layers.
